reasoning_traces.think:
The core challenge is converting public ESPN scoreboard data into deterministic settlement outcomes for user picks. This requires resolving ambiguous game states (e.g., totals vs spreads) and handling missing or invalid data without leaking information across bets. The two defects found—coercion of null to zero and improper total resolution—are classic edge-case failures in weakly typed languages. By introducing `strictNumber()` and enforcing total-resolution-first ordering, the system enforces a hard boundary: any incomplete game state yields a void, preventing spurious settlement. The Brier score measures calibration of stated probabilities against binary outcomes, while CLV tracks linear profit/loss under a fixed-size hedge. Together they form a minimal but complete verification suite: the daemon must produce identical void/win/loss classifications regardless of whether it uses paid or free paths, differing only in the presence of closing prices.
